hero_title: Unit 10 · You're supposed to shake hands.

knowledge.t: 单元话题 · 风俗与得体行为 (customs)
knowledge.d: 本单元围绕各国 customs(风俗习惯)与不同场合“该做什么、不该做什么”展开：见面礼仪(第一次见面怎么问候)、拜访礼仪、时间观念、餐桌礼仪。Language Goal: Talk about customs and what you are supposed to do. 核心句型：be supposed to do / be expected to do(应该、按理应做)+ It's impolite/important to do sth(做某事是不礼貌的/重要的)。单元话题句：You're supposed to shake hands.(你应该握手。)

knowledge.t: be supposed to do = should do · 应该做某事
knowledge.d: 结构：主语 + be(am/is/are；过去 was/were)+ supposed to + 动词原形。肯定表“应该做”：You're supposed to arrive on time.(你应该准时到达。) You're supposed to shake hands.(你应该握手。) 否定在 be 后加 not，表“不应该做”= shouldn't do：You're not supposed to smoke here.(你不应该在这里吸烟。) 疑问句把 be 提到句首：Am I supposed to wear jeans?(我应该穿牛仔裤吗?) 过去时表“本应该做(常含没做到)”：I was supposed to arrive at 7:00, but I arrived at 8:00.

knowledge.t: 同义表达 · be expected to do
knowledge.d: be expected to do sth 意为“按习俗/常理应当、被期望做某事”，与 be supposed to do 意思基本相同，可互换。例句(1c 对话)：A: What are people in Korea supposed to do when they meet for the first time? B: They're supposed to bow. 而 In the United States, they're expected to shake hands. Grammar Focus：—Am I supposed to wear jeans? —No, you're expected to wear a suit and tie. 两者后都接动词原形；expected 更强调“大家普遍预期如此”。比较：You're supposed to be there at noon. = You're expected to be there at noon.

knowledge.t: 见面礼仪 · 各国第一次见面怎么做 (1a/1b/2d)
knowledge.d: 第一次见面各国习惯不同：日本——鞠躬(初次见面通常 bow；1b 中日本人 Yoshi: We bow.)；韩国——同样鞠躬(And in Korea we also bow.)；巴西——有时亲吻脸颊(kiss)；美国、墨西哥及多数西方国家——握手(shake hands；1b 中墨西哥人 Rodrigo: In Mexico, we shake hands.)；法国——见面时互相亲吻脸颊两侧(2d: French people are supposed to kiss when they see each other.)。课文 2d：约翰向日本男孩 Sato 伸出手，Sato 却鞠了躬——That's how people in Japan are expected to greet each other. It's impolite if you don't bow.(在日本，见面不鞠躬是不礼貌的。)

knowledge.t: 准时文化 · 瑞士 vs 哥伦比亚 (3a 对比阅读)
knowledge.d: 瑞士学生 Marc(洛桑)：In Switzerland, it's very important to be on time.(在瑞士守时非常重要。) We're the capital of clocks and watches, after all!(毕竟我们是钟表之都!) 约好 noon 见面就 expected to be there at noon；迟到哪怕 15 分钟，朋友就可能 get mad；所以他 make an effort to be on time(努力守时)，认为 it's impolite to keep others waiting；而且从不未打电话就登门(never visit a friend's house without calling first)，见朋友几乎总先 make plans。哥伦比亚学生 Teresa(卡利)：We're pretty relaxed about time.(我们对时间相当放松。) 不喜欢 rush around(匆匆忙忙)，赴约稍晚一点没关系(don't mind if people are a little late)，珍惜与家人朋友共处的时光(value the time)，有空常直接 drop by 朋友家，不必提前约。→ 3a 答案：在哥伦比亚，晚餐晚到 15 分钟是可以接受的。

knowledge.t: 餐桌礼仪小测验 · 世界各地 (Section B 1a)
knowledge.d: 课本 1a 判断正误：①印度——应该用手抓饭吃(In India, you're supposed to eat with your hands.)，T；②中国——不该把筷子插进食物里(not supposed to stick your chopsticks into the food)，T；③韩国——最年幼的人被期待先动筷(the youngest person is expected to start eating first)，F(应是最年长者先吃)；④法国——面包应放在桌上(not on the plate)，T；⑤中国——用筷子敲空碗不礼貌(it's impolite to use your chopsticks to hit an empty bowl)，T。

knowledge.t: 中国的餐桌礼仪 · Steve 的中国之行 (Section B 1b/1c)
knowledge.d: Steve 将去中国留学，朋友 Yang Ming 告诉他中国的餐桌礼仪：不要把筷子插进食物/米饭里(You're not supposed to stick your chopsticks into your food.)；用筷子指着任何人是不礼貌的(It's impolite to point at anyone with your chopsticks.)；同桌有老人在场时不应先动筷(You shouldn't start eating first if there are older people at the table.)。归纳：插筷、用筷指人、敲空碗是中式餐桌“三忌”。

knowledge.t: Section B 2b · 林月 (Lin Yue) 在法国的餐桌挑战
knowledge.d: 阅读是 Lin Yue 写给 Laura 的信：她在法国的交换生活很愉快，寄宿家庭 go out of their way to make her feel at home(费尽心思让她有宾至如归之感)，祖母还特地学做中餐；她最大的挑战是餐桌礼仪(learning how to behave at the dinner table)：面包不能放盘子里，要放在桌上(not supposed to put your bread on your plate — supposed to put it on the table!)；除了面包，不能用手指拿任何食物吃，连水果也要切碎用叉子吃；说自己吃饱了是不礼貌的(It's impolite to say you're full.)，不想再吃就说 That was delicious.；手肘不能放桌上(not supposed to put your elbows on the table)。她 gradually getting used to it(逐渐习惯)，不再觉得法国风俗奇怪。

knowledge.t: 句型 It's + 形容词 + to do sth
knowledge.d: 句型：It's + impolite/polite/important/necessary + (for sb) + to do sth，意为“做某事是(不)礼貌的/(不)重要的”。it 是形式主语，真正的主语是后面的不定式 to do。Grammar Focus 例句：Is it impolite to keep others waiting? Yes, it's very impolite to keep others waiting.(让别人等着是非常不礼貌的。) Is it important to be on time? Yes, it's important to be on time.(守时很重要。) 课本 3a 还有 it's polite for boys to shake hands and for girls to kiss each other on the side of the face；也可用 It's impolite if you don't bow. 的 if 从句形式。

词汇：custom 风俗；bow 鞠躬；kiss 亲吻；greet 问候；relaxed 放松的(be relaxed about time 对时间不紧张)；value 重视/价值；drop by 顺便拜访；noon 正午；mad 生气的(get mad 生气)；effort 努力(make an effort to do 努力做)；passport 护照；chalk 粉笔(clean the chalk off the blackboard 擦掉黑板上的粉笔字)；northern 北部的(northern coast 北部海岸)；season 季节；knock 敲(门)(knock before entering 进门先敲门)；eastern 东部的；worth 值得的(It is worth the trouble. 值得费这番工夫)；manner 方式/礼貌(table manners 餐桌礼仪；mind your manners 注意礼貌)。短语：be supposed to 应该；shake hands 握手；drop by 顺便拜访；after all 毕竟；get mad 生气；make an effort 努力；stick...into 把……插入；go out of one's way (to do) 特意/费尽心思(做)；get used to (doing) 习惯(做)；gradually 逐渐地。

questions.q: —What are people in Korea supposed to do when they meet for the first time? —They're supposed to ____, just like in Japan.
questions.exp: 对话仿 1c：在韩国，第一次见面要鞠躬。课本 1b：日本人 Yoshi 说 We bow.(我们鞠躬)，韩国人 Kim 说 And in Korea we also bow.(在韩国我们也鞠躬。) 韩国、日本初次见面通常鞠躬(bow)。

questions.q: In Brazil, people sometimes ____ each other when they meet for the first time.
questions.exp: 课本 1b 听力原句：in Brazil, people sometimes kiss.(在巴西，人们有时亲吻脸颊。) 注意区分：日本/韩国初次见面 bow，美国 shake hands，巴西有时 kiss。

questions.q: In the United States, when people meet for the first time, they're ____ to shake hands.
questions.exp: 1c 对话原句：In the United States, they're expected to shake hands. be expected to do = 按习俗应当、被期望做某事，与 be supposed to do 同义，后接动词原形。

questions.q: In France, you're not supposed to eat anything with your ____ except bread, not even fruit.
questions.exp: 2b 林月的信原句：you're not supposed to eat anything with your hands except bread, not even fruit.(除了面包，不能用手拿任何食物吃，连水果也不行——要切碎用叉子吃。) 中西餐桌礼仪差异之一。

questions.q: You're supposed to ____ on time, so please don't be late.
questions.exp: be supposed to 后接动词原形：You're supposed to arrive on time.(你应该准时到达。) = You should arrive on time. arrive on time 准时到达。

questions.q: You're not supposed to ____ here. Look at the sign: No Smoking.
questions.exp: 否定式 be not supposed to do = shouldn't do(不应该)：You're not supposed to smoke here.(你不应该在这里吸烟。) not 加在 be 动词之后，to 后仍接动词原形。

questions.q: Maria ____ supposed to arrive at 7:00, but she arrived at 8:00.
questions.exp: 课文 2a：I was supposed to arrive at 7:00, but I arrived at 8:00. 讲述过去的事用 was/were supposed to(本应该……)；Maria 是第三人称单数，用 was。

questions.q: —Am I supposed to wear jeans to the dinner? —No, you're ____ to wear a suit and tie.
questions.exp: Grammar Focus 原句：No, you're expected to wear a suit and tie.(不，你按习俗应该穿西装打领带。) be expected to = be supposed to；一般疑问句把 be 提到句首：Am I supposed to wear jeans?

questions.q: In Switzerland, people think it's impolite ____ others waiting.
questions.exp: It's impolite to do sth(做某事不礼貌)，it 是形式主语，to do 才是真正主语。3a 原文：I think it's impolite to keep others waiting.(我认为让别人等着是不礼貌的。) 所以瑞士人守时。

questions.q: In Switzerland, if you're even 15 minutes late, your friend may ____.
questions.exp: 3a 原文：If you're even 15 minutes late, your friend may get mad.(哪怕迟到 15 分钟，你的朋友都可能生气。) 所以瑞士人 make an effort to be on time(努力守时)。get mad = 变得生气。

questions.q: Switzerland is the capital of clocks and watches, ____!
questions.exp: 3a 原文：We're the capital of clocks and watches, after all!(毕竟我们是钟表之都!) after all 毕竟。at all 根本(用于否定/疑问)，above all 最重要的是，first of all 首先。

questions.q: In Colombia, people are pretty ____ about time. They don't like to rush around.
questions.exp: 3a 哥伦比亚学生 Teresa 原句：We're pretty relaxed about time.(我们对时间相当放松。) 与瑞士人的守时形成对比——哥伦比亚人赴约稍迟到没关系，不喜欢 rush around(匆匆忙忙)。

questions.q: In Colombia, people often just ____ their friends' homes if they have time. They don't have to make plans first.
questions.exp: 3a 原文：We often just drop by our friends' homes if we have time.(有空时我们常直接顺路去朋友家。) drop by 顺便拜访，直接接地点；对比：瑞士人从不未打电话就登门(never visit a friend's house without calling first)。

questions.q: In China, you're not supposed to stick your chopsticks ____ the food.
questions.exp: Section B 1c 原句：You're not supposed to stick your chopsticks into your food.(不应该把筷子插进食物里。) stick A into B 把 A 插入 B 中；把筷子竖直插进米饭被认为不吉利、不礼貌。

questions.q: It's impolite to ____ at anyone with your chopsticks at the dinner table.
questions.exp: 1c 原句：It's impolite to point at anyone with your chopsticks.(用筷子指着任何人是不礼貌的。) point at sb/sth 指着某人/某物，介词 at 不能漏。

questions.q: In France, you're not supposed to put your ____ on the table while eating.
questions.exp: 2b 林月的信原句：you're not supposed to put your elbows on the table.(不能把手肘放在桌子上。) 别记反：在法国，面包恰恰要放在桌上——put your bread on the table, not on your plate! 法国不用筷子，故 chopsticks 不选。

flashcards.q: be supposed to do sth 是什么意思?
flashcards.a: 应该做某事，相当于 should do。结构：be(am/is/are/was/were)+ supposed to + 动词原形。例：You're supposed to arrive on time.(你应该准时到达。) 否定：be not supposed to do(不应该)；同义：be expected to do。

flashcards.q: You're supposed to shake hands. 怎么理解?
flashcards.a: 你应该(跟人)握手。单元核心句，用于“第一次见面该做什么”的话题。疑问：What are you supposed to do when you meet someone for the first time? 否定：You're not supposed to kiss.(你不应该亲吻。)
不应该做某事 = shouldn't do。否定加在 be 动词后：You're not supposed to smoke here.(你不应该在这里吸烟。) 变否定、疑问全靠 be 动词，不能加 do/does/did。

flashcards.q: I was supposed to arrive at 7:00, but I arrived at 8:00. 什么意思?
flashcards.a: 我本应该 7 点到，但 8 点才到。过去时间用 was/were supposed to，常带“本该做却没做”的意味(课文 2a 中 Maria 赴美国家宴迟到一小时)。现在的情况则用 am/is/are supposed to。

flashcards.q: 各国第一次见面做什么?
flashcards.a: 日本、韩国：bow 鞠躬(初次见面通常鞠躬)；巴西：sometimes kiss 亲吻脸颊；美国、墨西哥及多数西方国家：shake hands 握手；法国：kiss each other on both sides of the face 亲吻双颊。表达：They're supposed/expected to bow / shake hands / kiss.

flashcards.q: In Switzerland, it's very important to be on time. 为什么?
flashcards.a: 在瑞士，守时非常重要。We're the capital of clocks and watches, after all!(毕竟我们是钟表之都!) 迟到 15 分钟朋友就可能 get mad；应 make an effort to be on time，认为 it's impolite to keep others waiting；从不未先打电话就去朋友家(never visit a friend's house without calling first)。

flashcards.q: In Colombia, people are pretty relaxed about time. 具体表现?
flashcards.a: 哥伦比亚人时间观念相当放松：赴宴稍晚一点没关系，不喜欢 rush around(匆匆忙忙)；他们 value 与家人朋友共处的时光；有空常直接 drop by 朋友家(drop by one's home = 顺便登门拜访)，不必提前 make plans。

flashcards.q: 中国餐桌礼仪：筷子怎么用才对?
flashcards.a: 不要把筷子插进食物/米饭里(not supposed to stick your chopsticks into the food)；用筷子指人不礼貌(it's impolite to point at anyone with your chopsticks)；用筷子敲空碗不礼貌；有老人在场不应先动筷(shouldn't start eating first)。顺带记住：在印度用手抓饭吃；韩国由最年长者先动筷。

flashcards.q: In France：面包该放哪儿? 能用手指拿吃的吗?
flashcards.a: 面包要放桌上而不是盘子里(put your bread on the table, not on the plate!)；除了面包不能用手指拿食物吃，连水果都要切好用叉子；说自己吃饱了(I'm full)不礼貌，应说 That was delicious.；手肘不能放桌上(not supposed to put your elbows on the table)。

be supposed to 应该；be expected to 被期望/理应；shake hands 握手；drop by 顺便拜访；after all 毕竟；get mad 生气；make an effort (to do) 努力(做)；table manners 餐桌礼仪；stick...into 把……插入；knock before entering 进门先敲门；go out of one's way (to do) 特意/费尽心思(做)；(gradually) get used to (doing) (逐渐)习惯(做)；be on time 准时。

errors.title: be supposed to 后漏 to 或误接非原形
errors.wrong: 写成 You are suppose to arrive on time. / She is supposed arriving at 7:00. / They are supposed arrived on time.
errors.right: 固定结构是 be supposed to do sth：suppose 后必须有 to，to 后接动词原形。正确：You're supposed to arrive on time.(你应该准时到达。) 记法：把 be supposed to 当整体短语看，相当于 should，后面永远接动词原形，不加 -ing、-ed。

errors.title: 变否定/疑问时误用 do/does/did
errors.wrong: 把“你不应该在这里吸烟”写成 You don't supposed to smoke here.；疑问句写成 Do you supposed to arrive at 7:00?
errors.right: be supposed to 的否定和疑问全靠 be 动词：否定 You're not supposed to smoke here.(= shouldn't smoke)；疑问 Are you supposed to arrive at 7:00? 一般现在时用 am/is/are，过去用 was/were(Was she supposed to be here at noon?)，绝不能加 do/does/did。

errors.title: 时态与“本应该”含义混淆
errors.wrong: 把过去的约定写成现在时：Yesterday I am supposed to meet him at noon, but I forgot. 或在叙述昨天时用 am/is/are supposed to。
errors.right: 过去时间用 was/were supposed to：Yesterday I was supposed to meet him at noon. 课文：I was supposed to arrive at 7:00, but I arrived at 8:00.(本应 7 点到却 8 点到，含“没做到”之意。) 现在时 am/is/are supposed to 只用于现在的情况：You're supposed to arrive on time.

errors.title: It's impolite to do 句型结构写错
errors.wrong: 写成 It's impolite doing to keep others waiting. / It's impolite keep others waiting. / It's impolite for keep others waiting.
errors.right: 句型是 It's + 形容词 + (for sb) + to do sth：it 是形式主语，真正主语是不定式 to do。It's impolite to keep others waiting.(让别人等不礼貌。) It's important to be on time. It's polite for boys to shake hands and for girls to kiss each other on the side of the face.(3a 原句) 不定式必须是 to do，不能用 doing 或光秃秃的动词。

errors.title: 固定搭配介词/动词张冠李戴
errors.wrong: 把“筷子插进食物”说成 stick your chopsticks at/on the food；把“用筷子指着人”说成 point anyone with your chopsticks(漏 at)；把“顺路去朋友家”说成 drop by at my friend's home；把“敲门”说成 knock the door。
errors.right: stick A into B 把 A 插入 B 里面(not supposed to stick your chopsticks into the food)；point at sb/sth 指着某人某物，at 不能丢(It's impolite to point at anyone with your chopsticks.)；drop by + 地点，中间不加介词(drop by my friend's home)；敲门是 knock on/at the door，或说 knock before entering(进门前先敲门)。

errors.title: 各国习俗想当然、张冠李戴
errors.wrong: 以为日本人初次见面也 kiss；以为在美国见面应该 bow；以为法国人把面包放在盘子里、手肘可以放桌上；或认为“In Korea, the youngest person is expected to start eating first”是对的。
errors.right: 以课本为准：日本、韩国初次见面 bow(鞠躬)；美国、墨西哥等 shake hands(握手)；巴西 sometimes kiss；法国餐桌礼仪——面包放桌上而不是盘子里，手肘不能放桌上；中、韩等国通常由最年长者先动筷，“最年幼者先动筷”是错的；在中国不能用筷子指着人、不能把筷子插进食物里。
